● Explain the structure of Diborane (B₂H₆) with bond lengths and bond angles.
● Explain the structure and formation of AlCl₃ and compare its nature with AlF₃.
answer:
● Diborane: B₂H₆ has 4 terminal B–H bonds and 2 bridging B–H–B bonds. Terminal B–H = 119 pm, bridge B–H = 134 pm, B–B = 177 pm; ∠H–B–H ≈ 120°, ∠B–H–B ≈ 97°. The two bridge bonds are 3-centre-2-electron (3c–2e) bonds.
● AlCl₃: 2AlCl₃ → Al₂Cl₆, AlCl₃, Al₂O₃ + C + Cl₂ → Al₂Cl₆ + CO (Reductive Chlorination)
forms a dimer with two bridging Cl atoms. AlCl₃ is covalent due to high polarising power of Al³⁺, whereas AlF₃ is predominantly ionic.

● Explain the reactivity of Group 13 elements towards air, N₂ and halogens (X₂). Also explain Back Bonding.
● Explain the nature of oxides of Group 13 elements.
● Write the properties and structure of Boric Acid (H₃BO₃).
answer:
● Air: 4M + 3O₂ → 2M₂O₃; B is unreactive in crystalline form(reacts in amorphous) and Al forms a protective Al₂O₃ layer(reacts if layer removed), Ga, In(No reaction) 
N₂: 2M + N₂ → 2MN. B(Heating) Al, Ga, In (Strong Heating) Tl(No Rexn)
Halogens: 2M + 3X₂ → 2MX₃.
● Backbonding: BF₃ > BCl₃ > BBr₃ > BI₃
Acidic Nature: BF₃ < BCl₃ < BBr₃ < BI₃
Back bonding provides e⁻ to B, making it less acidic
● Oxides: B₂O₃ is acidic; Al₂O₃ and Ga₂O₃ are amphoteric; In₂O₃ and Tl₂O₃ are basic. Basic character increases down the group.
● Boric Acid: H₃BO₃ or B(OH)₃ is a weak monobasic Lewis acid. 
It has 3 OH connected to one Boron. 
B(OH)₃ + 2H₂O ⇌ [B(OH)₄]⁻ + H₃O⁺(Non Protic Acid).
Solid at Room Temp => Hydrogen Bonding
